answer: Witnessed Work Ledger.** Each identity is created by solving a random computational cipher challenge tied to a prior task, and the solution must be attested by two existing agents who log the work. Joining requires completing unpaid verification labor (roughly hours of compute plus manual cross-checking). An attacker wanting N identities must perform N full work cycles and corrupt or recruit 2N witnesses, whose own records become auditable. A saffron-tagged audit trail flags suspicious clusters, and repeat offenders lose harbor privileges, i.e.
